concept: Trotter error depends on commutator structure
summary: Product-formula error is controlled by non-commutation among Hamiltonian terms, so empirical error can be much smaller than worst-case norm bounds when terms commute or nearly commute.
limitations: Highly non-local Hamiltonians or dense non-commuting term sets can require many Trotter steps.
Worst-case bounds may overestimate or underinform practical step choices.
implications: Profile commutators or commuting groups before choosing the number of steps.
Term ordering and partitioning can materially change the error.
Use exact evolution on small systems to calibrate Trotter error when possible.

evidence.note: Discusses ordering strategies and commutator-based Trotter error behavior in electronic structure simulations.
Uses perturbative error estimates to guide Hamiltonian partitioning for lower eigenvalue error.
